findings.breaking_input: A router row with `max_attempts: 1`, first driver mock returning `__failure: {class: "transport"}`.
findings.why: The chain terms are only checked inside `nextHop` for the NEXT attempt; the FIRST attempt always runs regardless of `max_attempts`. A row declaring `max_attempts: 1` still dispatches one driver invocation and records a hop, so the term cannot bind its own first attempt. The 'refuse before spend' claim is false for the first attempt. The prior finding L5 identified this exact defect; the diff does not add a check of terms before the first attempt, so it is not fixed.
findings.fix: Consult `max_attempts` before the first dispatch (e.g. refuse a row whose `max_attempts < 1` or, per ADR-0228 item 6 counting every attempt, make `max_attempts: 1` mean the initial attempt is allowed but no hop; more precisely decide the first attempt with the same termsCheck the hops use).
findings.twin_of: A guard on one of N entry points
